title: Universal Semantic Logger Schema
description: Framework-agnostic semantic logging schema. Context types and their schemas are defined by applications, not by this logging framework

open.description: Top-level open operations in chronological order. Each entry may carry its own nested children.

close.description: Top-level close operations, parallel in shape to `open`.

events.description: Events that occurred within specific operations - each event's openId indicates the hierarchical scope/position where the event happened. Events are positioned within the operation hierarchy through openId references, enabling precise attribution and scope analysis for performance tracking and debugging

type.description: Application-defined event type (e.g., cache_operation, database_query, external_api)

context.description: Application-specific event data conforming to the referenced schema

links.description: Web Links for semantic relationships - extends JSON Schema with hypermedia concepts for AI understanding. While not part of JSON Schema specification, these links provide semantic context and relationships between log entries, following RFC 8288 Web Linking principles. Enables AI to understand contextual relationships, dependencies, and semantic connections that pure data structure cannot express

rel.description: Link relationship type following RFC 8288 Web Linking

title.description: Human-readable title for the link relationship

type.description: Media type hint for the linked resource

examples.title: External API failure that triggered this error

openEntry.description: Application-defined open context with optional sibling children.

type.description: Application-defined context type (e.g., http_request, database_query, business_logic)

context.description: Application-specific context data conforming to the referenced schema

open.description: Nested child operations in chronological order.

closeEntry.description: Application-defined close context; mirrors an openEntry and carries child closes in parallel.

type.description: Application-defined context type (e.g., http_response, database_result, business_complete)

context.description: Application-specific context data conforming to the referenced schema

profile.description: Profile data attributed to this specific operation (wall time plus per-segment Xdebug/XHProf captures). Present when DevSemanticLogger produced the log.

close.description: Nested child closes in the order their opens closed.

operationId.description: Unique operation identifier following semantic naming convention: {type}_{sequence_number}

openIdReference.description: References a parent operation ID for hierarchical correlation - establishes position within operation tree. Creates parent-child relationships enabling complete request flow analysis and performance attribution

contextType.description: Application-defined context type identifier. Applications define their own context types through individual schema files

operationProfile.description: Profile data for a single operation (open/close pair).

wallTime.description: Wall time for this operation in seconds

xdebug.description: Per-segment Xdebug trace references captured while this operation was active. Empty when Xdebug trace was not available.

source.description: Path to the Xdebug trace file on disk for this segment (a .gz suffix indicates a gzip-compressed trace)

xhprof.description: Per-segment XHProf snapshot references captured while this operation was active. Empty when XHProf was not available.

source.description: Path to the XHProf snapshot file on disk for this segment

oneOf.description: Relative path to local schema file

schemaUrl.description: Context schema reference for AI-human understanding alignment. While humans naturally understand what this context represents, AI needs explicit schema guidance to achieve the same level of comprehension about data structure, constraints, and business meaning. Supports both absolute URLs and relative file paths.
schemaUrl.$comment: Bridge: Humans intuitively understand context meaning; AI uses this schema reference to gain equivalent understanding.
